packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- My standing context (a memory index loaded at session start, not the packet) mentions a "Stams pilot" in a fragment-identification project. The images themselves carry pencil shelfmarks "Stams, STA, Frg. 217_1r" / "217-1v" and the strip "Frg. 217_2r" / "217_2v". No proposed identification of the work or author was revealed to me, and I have not tried to identify it. The text contains its own rubrics (e.g. "De sancto bricio epo", "De nomine", "De sca elizabet"); those are read from the image, not supplied.
- I did nothing beyond the brief: I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..020 in this directory (I did list the directory to find the file names; I did not open packet.json).
- Text lost to trimming/damage is marked [cut] or [illegible]; I have not restored it. Expansions in ( ) are my proposals from visible abbreviation marks.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 = overview of one opened bifolium (face labelled 217_1r), landscape, two pages side by side, each one column of ~40+ lines, brown ink, gothic textualis bookhand, ruled. Left page heavily stained (brown water/glue staining over the right half and lower area); left edge of left page is cropped so the first letters of many lines are cut or survive only as fragments outside the fold line. Bottom of left page trimmed obliquely (corners cut). Right page cleaner in its upper half (a pale rectangle where something was once pasted), stained lower half; outer right edge trimmed so line ends are partly lost.
- Right page: red rubric at line end "De sancto bricio epo" and a large red-and-ink initial B (about 3 lines high) with pen flourish; red touches on some capitals. Marginal notes on the right outer margin are minute cursive scraps (partly cut).
- Left page: two capitals touched in red (Tunc, Prefectus, Non, Oremus).
- image-011 = overview of the other face (217_1v), same bifolium, photographed with glass weights. Left page: red rubric "De nomine" with a large red initial E (~3 lines), a boxed red-framed phrase "in pace quieuit" ending the preceding chapter, a red paragraph mark, a second red rubric "De sca elizabet" and a large red initial E (~4 lines). Some short words in the left margin beside the E initial ("nobile", others) look like marginal additions/corrections. Right page: one red paragraph mark/initial C mid-page ("Cum itaq(ue) ..."), red-touched T near bottom.
- Some lines are underlined (left page of 1r near bottom; right page of 1r near bottom); this looks like later underlining in the same brown ink, not rubrication.
- image-010 and image-020 = overviews of a narrow separate strip (Frg. 217_2r / 2v), ~9-10 lines of a column, only a few letters per line. No native-resolution tiles of the strip were supplied, so it is read only tentatively.
- Interpretation (tentative): continuous prose narrative, chapter-divided with rubricated titles; no gloss/commentary layout visible.
- Overlap: tiles 002-005 run down the 1r left page, 006-009 down the 1r right page, 012-015 down the 1v left page, 016-019 down the 1v right page. Each tile repeats the last ~2-3 lines of the previous tile; repeated lines are marked "overlap" and not re-transcribed.

SELECTED AREAS: I read essentially all legible lines of all four pages from the tiles. Unread/weak: left-cropped line beginnings of 1r left page; stained right ends of 1r left page lines; the damaged top line of 1r right page; trimmed bottom lines of each page; the strip (overview resolution only). A higher-resolution tile of the strip and a raking/UV view of the stained right half of 1r left page would help.
